questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'a piece of cake' mean?
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' refers to a task that is very easy to do.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to break the ice' mean?
options: To ease the initial awkwardness in a meeting
questions.explanation: Breaking the ice means doing or saying something to relax people meeting for the first time.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: The idiom comes from working by lamplight late at night.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to bite the bullet' mean?
options: To face a difficult situation bravely
questions.explanation: Biting the bullet means accepting something unpleasant with courage.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: Something good that at first seemed bad
questions.explanation: An apparent misfortune that turns out to be beneficial.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' mean?
questions.explanation: It means to say or do precisely the right thing.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag' mean?
options: To reveal a secret by mistake
questions.explanation: It means disclosing a secret, usually carelessly.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'once in a blue moon' mean?
questions.explanation: A 'blue moon' is an infrequent event, so the phrase means very seldom.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to beat about the bush' mean?
options: To avoid coming to the point
questions.explanation: It means talking around a subject without addressing it directly.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to call it a day' mean?
options: To stop working for the time being
questions.explanation: Calling it a day means deciding to stop an activity.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'a red-letter day' mean?
questions.explanation: From the old custom of marking feast days in red on calendars.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to be in hot water' mean?
questions.explanation: Being in hot water means facing trouble or disapproval.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to cry wolf' mean?
options: To complain about danger that is real
questions.explanation: From Aesop's fable of the shepherd boy whose false alarms led to his real cry being ignored.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to turn a blind eye' mean?
questions.explanation: It means deliberately ignoring something wrong.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'the lion's share' mean?
questions.explanation: From Aesop: the lion took the largest portion.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom 'to add fuel to the fire' mean?
options: To make a bad situation worse
questions.explanation: Adding fuel to the fire means aggravating a conflict.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: She has been living here for 2015.
She has been living here since 2015.
questions.explanation: With 'since' + a point in time, use the present perfect (continuous): 'has been living'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Neither the teacher nor the students is present.
Neither the teacher or the students were present.
Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Neither the teacher nor the students were present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students' → 'were').

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Each of the boys have a bicycle.
Each of the boys has a bicycle.
Each of the boys are having a bicycle.
Each of the boy has a bicycle.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has'; 'of the' requires the plural noun 'boys'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He is one of best players who have ever played for Pakistan.
He is one of the best players who has ever played for Pakistan.
He is one of the best players who have ever played for Pakistan.
He is one of the best player who has ever played for Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The relative clause refers to 'players' (plural), so 'who have'; 'one of the' needs a plural noun.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He did not went to school yesterday.'
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did', use the base form of the verb: 'did not go'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The news are very disturbing.'
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'I am looking forward to meet you.'
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: 'meeting'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Scarcely had he reached the station than the train left.'
questions.explanation: The correct pairing is 'scarcely … when' (or 'no sooner … than').

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The furnitures in this room are old.
The furniture in this room are old.
The furnitures in this room is old.
The furniture in this room is old.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable: no plural form, singular verb.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Unless you do not work hard, you will not pass.'
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so adding 'do not' creates a double negative: 'Unless you work hard…'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I were you, I will accept the offer.
If I was you, I will accept the offer.
If I am you, I would accept the offer.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: Hypothetical conditionals use the subjunctive 'were' with 'would'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is senior from me by two years.
She is senior to me by two years.
She is senior than me by two years.
She is more senior than me by two years old.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as senior, junior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'I prefer tea than coffee.'
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to': 'I prefer tea to coffee'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The weather was such bad that we stayed indoors.
The weather was so bad as we stayed indoors.
The weather was too bad that we stayed indoors.
The weather was so bad that we stayed indoors.
questions.explanation: 'So' + adjective + 'that' expresses result; 'such' is used with a noun phrase ('such bad weather').

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Accommodation has double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: He is fond ___ reading novels.
questions.explanation: 'Fond of' is the fixed collocation.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: The train arrived ___ the station on time.
questions.explanation: 'Arrive at' is used for a specific place such as a station; 'arrive in' for a city or country.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She was accused ___ theft.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse someone of' something; compare 'charged with'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: He insisted ___ paying the bill.
questions.explanation: 'Insist on' + gerund.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She congratulated him ___ his success.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate someone on' something is the standard collocation.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: I have been waiting for you ___ two hours.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time; 'since' with a point in time.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: The two brothers differ ___ each other in temperament.
questions.explanation: 'Differ from' a person or thing; 'differ with' means to disagree with someone.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She is good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: 'Good at' a subject or skill.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: He was absorbed ___ his work and did not hear the bell.
questions.explanation: 'Absorbed in' means fully occupied with.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She is ___ honest woman.
questions.explanation: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: He is ___ European.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a consonant 'y' sound, so 'a'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ Indus is the longest river in Pakistan.
questions.explanation: Names of rivers take the definite article: the Indus.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: Unique things such as the sun, the moon and the earth take the definite article.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She plays ___ piano beautifully.
questions.explanation: Musical instruments take 'the' after 'play': play the piano, play the flute.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ___.
questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the match.
questions.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: She ___ in Lahore for ten years before she moved to Karachi.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events (living, then moving) uses the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: If he had studied harder, he ___ the examination.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A person who can speak many languages'.
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows several languages; 'bilingual' means two.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A place where birds are kept'.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A person who does not believe in the existence of God'.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A drug used to treat bacterial infections'.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A government by the people'.
questions.explanation: Democracy: rule by the people; autocracy: by one person; oligarchy: by a few.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A person who walks in sleep'.
questions.explanation: A somnambulist sleepwalks; an insomniac cannot sleep.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'That which cannot be read'.
questions.explanation: Illegible means unreadable; ineligible means not qualified.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A word that is opposite in meaning to another'.
questions.explanation: An antonym has the opposite meaning; a synonym the same meaning.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'The study of the human mind and behaviour'.
questions.explanation: Psychology studies the mind; physiology studies bodily functions.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A speech made without preparation'.
questions.explanation: Extempore means spoken or done without preparation.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'One who is present everywhere'.
questions.explanation: Omnipresent: everywhere; omnipotent: all-powerful; omniscient: all-knowing.

questions.prompt: Choose the one word for: 'A list of the books and articles referred to in a work'.
questions.explanation: A bibliography lists sources; a glossary defines terms; an anthology is a collection of writings.
